episodes.170553: Localized flash flooding was reported over the southeast portion of the Cameron Peak burn area near Glen Haven.  Larimer County Road 43 was impassable with floodwaters overtopping the roadway near Streamside Drive.
episodes.170556: The end of July continued to be busy for meteorologists at the Albuquerque National Weather Service Office as numerous thunderstorms impacted the area on July 30, 2022. With well above normal moisture available in the atmosphere, these thunderstorms were robust and very capable of producing heavy rainfall. Several flash flooding reports were received, including in the Rio Rancho and Edgewood areas.
episodes.170557: Monsoon season got off to an early start, and that momentum continued throughout the entire month of July with yet another very busy and active day on July 31, 2022. Per usual, thunderstorms developed early in the day across the high terrain areas before becoming more widespread throughout the evening. Many of these thunderstorms were capable of producing heavy rain which resulted in flash flooding reports across the area. The Calf Canyon burn scar was hit again with flash flooding and debris flow near Gascon while flash flooding across western New Mexico forced the closure of a few roadways.
episodes.170605: An upper level high pressure center over the Great Basin provided for an easterly flow aloft over central California which allowed form enough mid/upper moisture to stream into the area for showers and thunderstorms to break out during the afternoon and evening. While several stations across the central California interior picked up between a hundredth of an inch and two tenths of an inch of rainfall, a few mountain locations that were impacted by heavier thunderstorms picked up more.
episodes.170719: Abundant monsoon moisture remained over the Four Corners region. This led to another round of showers and thunderstorms across western Colorado. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain. Some storms produced localized debris flows in Pitkin and Ouray counties with flooding reported in Montrose County.
episodes.170721: Abundant monsoon moisture remained over the Four Corners region. This led to another round of showers and thunderstorms across southeast Utah. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain. Another debris flow occurred on the Pack Creek Fire burn scar as a result of a large amount of heavy rain in a short period of time.
episodes.170722: Abundant monsoon moisture remained over the Four Corners region. This led to another round of showers and thunderstorms across southwest Colorado. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain. One such storm wiped out a portion of the road leading from the El Diente Peak trailhead from flash flooding.
episodes.170856: Afternoon thunderstorms developed over far eastern Montana during the afternoon.  One storm was strong enough to reach severe levels with a strong downburst wind.
episodes.171249: Localized flooding issues arose for the final few days of July in West Virginia as daily showers and thunderstorms developed. These storms were generally slow moving, contributing to heavy and prolonged periods of rainfall. High water inundation onto local roads were observed in parts of central West Virginia during the course of these events.
episodes.171250: A weak disturbance crossed over northeast Kentucky on July 31st at the same time a warm front migrated northward at the surface. These two features provided the needed support for showers and thunderstorms that developed in the late morning time frame. Flash flooding resulted in Boyd County with blocked roadways and a quick response of local creeks.
episodes.171293: Several days of monsoon thunderstorms impacted the mountains and High Desert in Southern California. The San Bernardino County Mountains were particularly hard hit. Torrential downpours led to flash flooding and debris flows, including over the El Dorado burn scar.
episodes.171477: A stalled frontal boundary and surface low pressure south of the state early Sunday morning began to slowly lift northward into the southeast and south-central portion of the state throughout the day. Showers and thunderstorms developed along the boundary and moved eastward. Since the system as whole showed very little forward progression, multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms ended up moving across the same locations multiple times, on top of already saturated soils. This ended up leading to multiple instances of flash flooding, specifically in Whitley and Pike Counties.
episodes.171891: A cluster of strong thunderstorms developed over the southern Nebraska Panhandle during the afternoon of the 31st. These storms ended up producing severe downburst winds around Sidney.
episodes.171914: A tropical upper-tropospheric trough (TUTT) low was moving westward across the northern Gulf of Mexico. This feature brought with it, abundant moisture throughout the column as well as a focus for storms to develop. As one of those moved northward from New Orleans into Lake Pontchartrain, its intensity was enhanced by a lingering land-breeze boundary. That storm quickly collapsed after it passed north of the boundary. When doing so, a burst of severe winds was sent out by the storm across Mid-Lake Pontchartrain.
episodes.172037: A wave of low pressure along a nearly stationary front positioned across southern Virginia, helped spawn scattered afternoon thunderstorms. A couple of these storms produced damaging winds in the Virginia Southside.
episodes.172300: A surface warm front located across north-central North Carolina tracked into Virginia by the afternoon and evening hours. At the same time, a mid-level disturbance tracked east from the Tennessee Valley into the North Carolina/Virginia region. Aided by copious moisture and favorable flow for isolated tornadoes/damaging winds, there was one single report of a tree down in Halifax County. Most storms stayed below severe limits, forming mainly along the warm front over the northeast Piedmont and northern Coastal Plain in the afternoon and evening. Additional storms pushed east into the western and central Piedmont overnight into August 1st, but stayed below severe limits.
episodes.172306: Two areas of severe weather developed during the evening and nighttime hours. The first area was along a cold front over northwest North Dakota, where strong thunderstorm wind gusts were the primary threat, with the strongest wind gust of 69 mph being reported at the Williston Airport in Williams County. The second area was over central North Dakota affecting Wells and Foster counties, where an area of thunderstorms produced strong thunderstorm winds and some large hail. The strongest reported wind gust in this area was 61 mph at the Carrington Airport in Foster County, while one inch diameter hail fell to the west of Hurdsfield in Wells County.
episodes.172418: Scattered thunderstorms with gusty winds moved over the James River on July 31.
episodes.172466: Daytime heating combined with divergence aloft associated with an easterly wave near the Arizona/New Mexico border promoted thunderstorm initiation across southeast Arizona during the afternoon of the 30th. Outflow boundaries generated from these thunderstorms raced northwest toward south-central Arizona, resulting in a dust storm in Pinal County where multiple instances of dense blowing dust less than 1/4 mile were reported. New thunderstorm development occurred along these boundaries with some thunderstorms becoming severe. Numerous instances of damaging winds were reported across the Phoenix area and down into northwest Pinal County, which included multiple downed trees and power poles. A very moist environment, with PWATs in excess of 1.80 allowed for thunderstorms to become efficient heavy rainfall producers. Rainfall amounts upwards of around 1.50 within an hour were reported during the event. There were multiple reports of flash flooding across northern parts of the Phoenix area, leading to several water rescues and making some roads impassable. Flash flooding also led to water and mud entering some apartments in north Phoenix causing extensive water damage. Isolated flash flooding occurred across Pinal, Gila, and Yuma Counties. No injuries were reported with this event.
episodes.172500: A strong upper-level ridge set up across the western U.S. with broad ridging extending eastward across the Ark-La-Tex region. However, slight weakening along the eastern extent of the ridge allowed for convection to become more likely with diurnal heating. At the surface, a weak frontal boundary located from along the middle Red River Valley eastward into central Arkansas had become nearly stationary. Along and south of the boundary, plentiful moisture characteristic of dew points mainly in the lower 70s were noted. Some lingering outflow boundaries were also present from earlier convection, and these features combined to help trigger an isolated severe thunderstorm during the early evening hours in Northeastern Panola County. This storm produced isolated damaging wind gusts just west of Bethany.
episodes.172645: A push of monsoonal moisture resulted in sporadic flash flooding and isolated microbursts for the end of the month of July.
episodes.172690: Scattered thunderstorms moved northwest across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. Heavy rain over the Bighorn Fire burn scar resulted in flash flooding in Finger Rock Canyon. Several homes and an assisted living facility were flooded in the Catalina Foothills. Flash flooding also occurred in Nogales and in western Pima County. Large hail and isolated wind damage were observed in parts of the Tucson Metro area.
episodes.172738: An upper-level disturbance lingering over the area in combination with MLCAPE of approximately 1000-1500 J/KG and DCAPE of around 1000 J/KG lead to the development of strong storms across portions of southern and central Arizona during the afternoon hours. Outflow winds led to areas of blowing dust with the more persistent storms leading to isolated flash flooding.
episodes.172802: A weak warm frontal passage aided convective downpours in a weak steering environment.
episodes.172842: A slowly advancing low pressure system off the coast and a ridging over the intermountain west allowed moisture in the mid-levels to advect into the central OR area. Increasing instability from hot temperatures allowed for a strong thunderstorm to develop near the the Madras, OR area in the afternoon.
episodes.172850: An isolated severe thunderstorm moved into the area overnight, bringing wind damage to portions of Eddy County.
episodes.172877: Deep monsoon moisture remained over northern Arizona with thunderstorms, heavy rain, and flash flooding.
episodes.172913: The stormy period which began on the 24th continued to bring severe weather and flash flooding through the end of the month.
episodes.172914: The stormy period which began on the 24th continued to bring severe weather and flash flooding through the end of the month.

episodes.172929: Deep monsoon moisture allowed the formation of thunderstorms with heavy rain and flash flooding across northern Arizona.
episodes.172930: Deep monsoon moisture allowed the formation of thunderstorms with heavy rain and flash flooding across northern Arizona.
episodes.172969: An isolated severe thunderstorm moved into Iredell County from the northwest during the early evening. Locally damaging wind gusts were reported in the northern part of the county.
episodes.173024: A warm front moved through Eastern North Carolina, with scattered thunderstorms on the evening of July 31st.  Some of these storms produced wind damage, especially toward the Crystal Coast.

events.narrative: The culverts backed up as a result of heavy rain from thunderstorms. This resulted in several inches of water and some embedded debris spilling over onto Racine and Sunshine Roads in Montrose.
Water flowing over road, with rocks and debris noted along State Route 247 at Northside.

An image showed a large branch of a tree snapped off and narrowly missed a home near Ocotillo Road and Meridian Road. A video taken in the area showed very strong winds estimated to be in excess of 60 mph. No injuries were reported.
Vehicle stuck in mud along State Route 247 and Meander Road.
Wind gusts up to 60 mph were measured with a handheld anemometer. Multiple 10-inch diameter Palo Verde trees were reported to have been knocked over in the area. No injuries were reported.
I-15 southbound and northbound lanes flooded.
A video showed a palm tree falling onto three vehicles at a car dealership resulting in damage to the vehicles. No injuries were reported.
The Big Sky Field Airport AWOS measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 66 mph.

Spring Creek was reported to be running approximately 8-9 ft in depth, impacting low water crossings through the creek. Over 2 of rain was reported to have fallen in the span of about an hour in this area. No damage or injuries were reported.

Forest Service Road 396 was closed between Stagecoach Trail and the Eads Wash Day Use Site and River Access Point due to unsafe road conditions from flash flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.

The Madras airport ASOS measured a wind gust of 67mph at 5:55pm. An NWS employee 1 mile southwest of Madras, OR also witnessed thunderstorm outflow winds that blew down fences, produced low visibilities in blowing dust, and also produced a gustnado in nearby farm fields.
SR 238 westbound was closed at milepost 41 due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
SR-247 closed at Rabbit Springs Road (northbound) due to flooding and debris flows.
An image showed a large tree that fell onto three parked vehicles at an apartment complex near 7th Avenue and Osborn Road. No injuries were reported.

Approximately 7-8 power poles were reported down along the Grand Canal, with many falling toward homes and crashing through cinder block walls. Another cinder block wall was knocked down after a metal shed blew out of the backyard of a home and into the canal. No injuries were reported.
Rain of 1.34 inch. Mesonet Yucaipa Ridge measured in one hour.
Rainfall of 1.20 inch measured in 45 minutes at Arrowbear.
Thunderstorm wind gusts were estimated by a trained spotter.
An image showed a large tree fell onto and destroyed a metal carport, with an SUV parked underneath. No injuries were reported.
A tree was downed along Highway 79 near Bethany.
Media live broadcast showed a snapped power pole near Cave Creek Road and Greenway Road. No injuries were reported.
An image showed a metal carport roof blown onto a couple of parked cars. No injuries were reported.

Flash flooding 4 SW Forest Falls. A car was reported stuck in flood waters at Oak Glen Road and Potato Canyon Road. Ten homes were shelter in place due to flash flooding of Potato Canyon from Birch Creek. Potato Canyon Road covered in mud and debris and eventually washed out at Birch Creek. Road closed from Saturday night into Sunday morning. Rainfall of 1.8 inch was measured at Yucaipa Ridge upstream, 1.2 of which occurred in one hour.

Images showed a gas station canopy knocked over at 7th Street and Coral Gables Drive, falling onto a vehicle. Nearby, images showed an uprooted tree approximately 1 ft in diameter fallen over onto a fence, tearing part of the fence down. No injuries were reported.
ASOS at Phoenix-Deer Valley Municipal Airport.

A video showed firefighters performing a swift water rescue after an SUV stalled in floodwaters when attempting to drive across a low water crossing along 7th Avenue between Greenway Parkway and Coral Gables Drive. At 1925MST, a nearby FCDMC stream gage exceeded bank full stage after recording a peak height of 8.07 ft and a peak flow of 5,080 cfs, which broke the record for this gage. No injuries were reported.

Up to 3 ft of water and mud entered some first floor apartments at Central Avenue and Bell Road after the drainage system was overcome. Some cars in the parking lot of the apartment were also damaged. No injuries were reported.
A video showed approximately 1-2 ft of water flowing across the road near 12th Street and Hatcher Road. No damage or injuries were reported.

Eagle Eye Road was closed between Salome Highway and US 60 due to flooding in multiple locations along the road. A FCDMC stream gage along Tiger Wash, which flows across an unbridged crossing along the road, briefly climbed above alarm stage after peaking at a height of 5.98 ft and a flow of 541 cfs. No damage or injuries were reported.
Thunderstorm wind gusts were estimated by emergency management.
Rainfall of 1.81 inch. Yucaipa Ridge daily total rainfall.
A video showed six cars stalled in floodwaters at the I-17 and Greenway Road underpass. No injuries were reported.
A video on social media showed approximately 6-8 of water flowing south down 16th Street next to Buffalo Ridge Park. No damage or injuries were reported.

Photos showed flooding across Scottsdale Road near Deer Valley Road, making the road impassable. Police were on scene to prevent people from attempting to cross the flooded roadway. No damage or injuries were reported.
Thunderstorm wind gusts were estimated by a trained spotter.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Antelope Canyon.  The popular tourist slot canyon was closed for at least a day so that the water could be removed and sand could be replaced.
A video showed a car stalled in floodwaters over two feet deep near 7th Street and Hearn Road. No injuries were reported.
A video showed Galloway Wash flowing over School House Road, making the road impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.
A FCDMC stream gage along Cave Creek climbed above alarm stage, peaking at 6.24 ft and 2,459 cfs at 1943MST.

Heavy rain of 3.5 to 4 inches caused flash flooding south of Clayton. A trained spotter reported that the heavy rain caused Carrizo Creek to overflow its banks. Standing water and debris was reported across area roadways and within fields. Damages are estimated.
All the low water crossings over Short Creek were flooded and closed.
Hwy 190 was flooded.
Image showed stalled SUV in floodwaters at a low water crossing along Cloud Road between 7th Street and 10th Street. No injuries were reported.

Thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall over the high terrain near the town of Hildale over the course of an hour, with Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 1-hour estimates of around 1 to 1.5 inches of rainfall. Light to moderate rain persisted for 2 to 3 hours thereafter. The rainfall resulted in a strong flow in Short Creek through Hildale and on into Colorado City. Dispatch from Colorado City reported all street crossings across the creek were closed due to flooding, and 3 feet of fast moving water was reported to be flowing across Hildale Street.
A video of flash flooding in Antelope Canyon was posted on social media.

Elevated flow in Skunk Creek led to the closure of a low water crossing along 19th Avenue between Desert Hills Drive and Irvine Road. A nearby FCDMC stream gage along Skunk Creek recorded a peak flow of 624 cfs and a peak height of 2.71 ft. No damage or injuries were reported.
Several large, 3 to 5 inch tree branches were broken down around a farmstead. Three sections of stock fencing were blown down. Time estimated based on radar.
The Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City flooded area farm lands. Homes in the area were threatened.

In the suburbs of Huntington, 5th Avenue was inundated with water, restricting vehicle access to homes. Other roads flooded as well within the city limits, including Virginia Avenue and Woodland Drive.
In Rockdale, Shopes Creek rose above its banks and spilled onto Route 538, restricting traffic through the area. Portions of Route 60 near Cannonsburg were also inundated with high water.
Route 854 at the intersection of KY 1654 was blocked due to flooding in the area.
High water surrounded the Spring Valley Public Safety Center, restricting access to the parking garage for a brief period of time.
A tree was reported down near the intersection of Ringwood Road and Heathsville Road.
The Weatherflow mesonet station at Mid Lake Pontchartrain recorded a thunderstorm wind gust of 36 knots or 41 mph.
Flooding of Wilson Hollow Road, both bridge and roadway being covered.
Water was reported out of the banks of Coon Creek and flowing over the road at Johns Branch.
Water was observed flowing over the road in front of Johns Oil (Lonesome Cedar Lane) in the community of Coal Run.
Drainage ditch overflowing with flooding on both sides of Highway 38 near Mitchell Lane.
Flooding on Highway 38 between Paradise and Maple Lane.
Debris and rocks across Highway 38 at Hill Ranch Road, where there was also water flowing across the road. Vehicles stuck on roadway, requiring rescue.
I-15 was flooded at Bailey Rd.
Highway 38 closed between Valley of the Falls to Lake Williams. Multiple cars stuck, requiring rescue west of Jenks Lake.
Water was observed flowing over Sukey Hollow Road near Saxton.
Six inches of water was observed flowing over Hwy 1804 at the I-75 overpass near Fairview.
The left hand lane of Hwy 25 was blocked under the I-75 overpass due to water flowing over the road.

Heavy rain of 0.4 inch along I-5 from San Juan Capistrano to Lake Forest. Small street flooding along freeway on/offramps and local intersections. Several small traffic incidents, slowing traffic along I-5.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 90 minutes caused Gunsight Wash to rise rapidly and flood/close Highway 85 near mile post 55.
Whitley County 911 dispatch reported that a water rescue took place along Little Wolf Creek Road near Mountain Ash.
Whitley County 911 dispatch reported that Kensee Hollow Road near Red Ash was washed out and active rescues were taking place for people who were trapped on the other side of the washed out road.
Hwy 190 was closed.
County Road 43 at Streamside Drive was impassable due to floodwaters from Miller Fork.
Laurel Fork Road observed high water as did other local roads in the county that afternoon.
A video showed flooding on Hwy 95 south of the solar farms.
Flooding washed large rocks onto Hwy 168.

While performing a search and rescue operation for an injured hiker at El Diente Peak, Dolores County Search and Rescue members narrowly escaped a portion of the road exiting the trailhead being washed out as a result of flash flooding from heavy rain.
A flash flood completely buried a vehicle in mud.
Several intersections along and near Hwy 160 were flooded over a foot deep.
Pond Creek was out of its banks and flowing across the back alley at Belfry Middle School.
Kelbaker Rd was flooded and severely damaged.
Hwy 127 was flooded with lots of rocks and debris in the road, and one vehicle was stuck in the water.
Onslow County 911 reported large limbs down near the intersection of Padgett road and Haws Run road.  The time was based on radar.
Onslow County 911 reported trees down near the intersection of Blue Creek road and Pony Farm road.  The time was based on radar.
Amateur radio relayed a report of wind gusts between 50 and 60 MPH at the intersection of Highway 17 and Western Boulevard in Jacksonville. The time was based on radar.
Amateur radio relayed reports of multiple large branches and limbs down at the intersection of Piney Green road and County Club road.  The time was based on radar.
Thunderstorm winds blew down three trees, one of which fell on a house.
